Gerván Dániel azt írta, a sofőr tudatában van annak, hogy a veszteséget és a hozzátartozók fájdalmát semmilyen szó nem enyhítheti, emellett tisztában van a baleset következményeivel és azok súlyával is. Arról is írt, hogy a busz vezetőjét megviselték a történtek, a feldolgozásában szakemberek nyújtanak neki segítséget. Az ügyvéd kiemelte, hogy az eljárás nagyon korai szakaszban van, így a nyomozás érdekeire figyelemmel nem osztanak meg további részleteket az ügyről, de tisztában vannak azzal, hogy az jelentős közérdeklődésre tart számot. A család további információkat a jövőben a jogi képviselőjükön keresztül oszt meg a nyilvánossággal. A lengyel zarándokokat szállító busz vasárnap hajnalban borult fel az M3-as autópályán Mezőkeresztesnél. Tizenkét ember meghalt , többen súlyosan megsérültek. A rendőrség elsődleges adatai szerint a sofőr feltehetően elaludt. Őt őrizetbe vették , halálos tömegszerencsétlenség gondatlan okozása miatt indult eljárás ellene . A férfit gyanúsítottként hallgatták ki, egyelőre nem tett vallomást. A Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén Vármegyei Főügyészség közleménye szerint a férfi nem volt a busz biztonságos vezetésére képes állapotban, fáradtságából kifolyólag elaludt. Az ügyészség álláspontja szerint a gyanúsított esetében fennáll a szökés és elrejtőzés, illetve a bizonyítás megnehezítésének veszélye, ezért a rendőrség előterjesztése alapján indítványt tett a bíróságnak a férfi letartóztatásának elrendelésére, letartóztatásáról kedden döntöttek. Péter Zagyi Tibor Bakró-Nagy Ferenc Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom “For many years they lied to us, claiming that the national holiday belonged to only one political side, but that’s over now,” Péter Magyar said in his address on October 23, as he greeted “the now truly independent Hungary.” Meanwhile, Viktor Orbán was photographed in Paris, so Fidesz celebrated without him. According to the former governing party, in a free country, those in authority do not threaten anyone with arrest, and there are no political prisoners—thus, the coming years will be fraught with struggle and immense hardship. The 70th anniversary of the Hungarian Revolution of 1956 in pictures. In keeping with tradition, the events on October 23rd began with a flag-raising ceremony in front of the Parliament building, followed by a military parade. António Costa, President of the European Council, Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, and Jens Stoltenberg, Norway’s Minister of Finance and former NATO Secretary General, were also in attendance at the Parliament’s formal session, where House Speaker Ágnes Forsthoffer said: “Today, the heart of the world beats in Budapest". According to President András Baka, the presence of foreign guests made the commemoration particularly meaningful, as the 70th anniversary of the Hungarian Revolution is of global significance and at the time, the revolution also contributed to the creation of European unity. During the state ceremony at Kossuth Square, the revolution that broke out 70 years ago was commemorated with fifty-six bell chimes. Just before Péter Magyar’s speech, Gripen jets flew over the square. “Anyone who makes excuses for an aggressor or would subject the nation to foreign empires has failed to understand the message of 1956,” Prime Minister Péter Magyar said in his nearly one-hour speech. He said there were thirteen glorious days when Hungarians united as one and demanded: “Russians, go home!” He also spoke about how “for many years they lied to us, claiming that the national holiday belonged to only one political side, but that is now over.” He said it would be good to leave our children a country we can be proud of. “This is our homeland, and we will do anything for it,” he said. Fidesz supporters organised a “Flag March”; the procession set off around noon from in front of the University of Technology and Economics to the sound of horsewhip cracks. It was led by a man dressed as a hussar, followed by men dressed as betyárs (19th century social bandit), and finally the participants of the march, who carried a 1,848-meter-long Hungarian flag. For a while, they marched along the lower embankment of Buda in complete silence. Then they began to sing patriotic songs. By the time they reached Bem Square, the crowd that had gathered was bigger than those seen at any of Fidesz’s rallies in recent months. Unlike in previous years, this time, Viktor Orbán did not deliver a commemorative address. Instead, he was sitting at a hotel terrace in Paris while his Facebook page live-streamed the event from Bem Square. There, speakers included Fidesz' parliamentary group leader János Bóka, former president János Áder; and historian Mária Schmidt. According to Áder, if he had to sum up in one word what people had had enough of in ’56, he would say “lies.” Dictatorship instead of democracy, servitude instead of freedom, poverty instead of prosperity, and a new nomenclature instead of equality. János Bóka spoke about there being no political police in a free country, and said that in such a country, those in power do not threaten anyone with arrest, no one is paraded in handcuffs at the behest of the authorities, and there are no political prisoners. In a free country, there is no attempt to eliminate the opposition. During his speech, Fidesz participants clashed with a few counter-protesters, who had to be protected by intervening police. Telex's reporters were also attacked. András Baka, Péter Magyar, and Ágnes Forsthoffer during the ceremonial raising of the national flag on the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Revolution at Kossuth Square in front of the Parliament Building on October 23, 2026 – Photo: Zoltán Máthé / MTI Mi Hazánk and its affiliated organizations held a commemoration at Corvin Köz, marking not only the 1956 uprising but also the 20th anniversary of the storming of the public television headquarters in 2006. Speakers included Előd Novák and László Toroczkai. The speeches mentioned the secret elite, globalists, LGBTQ lobby groups, and interference in elections, but the names of Ursula Von der Leyen and Péter Magyar were also mentioned numerous times. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Photograph: Leah Millis/Reuters View image in fullscreen Jensen Huang with Donald Trump at an 'Investing in America' event in Washington, on 30 April 2025. Photograph: Leah Millis/Reuters Nvidia Analysis The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence Robert Tait in Washington Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran Tue 24 Nov 2026 09.00 EST Last modified on Tue 24 Nov 2026 11.01 EST Share Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view. Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang , was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geo-strategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race. The woman, Alice Huang – no blood relation of Jensen – was also responsible for buying $4.8bn worth of Nvidia’s highly sensitive AI chips in her capacity as head of a Singapore-based technology company, Megaspeed. The chips were then diverted to China, despite US export restrictions forbidding such sales to a country Washington regards as a key strategic adversary. The president was inactive even after Marco Rubio, the secretary of state and national security – and one of the administration’s renowned “China hawks” – repackaged the intelligence into a classified report last May warning of the geopolitical risks posed by the relationship. “It’s clear that the White House was warned, had adequate opportunities to take action against what was an emerging and then eventually very clear chip diversion network that was emerging under Megaspeed and other Southeast Asian offshore data farms – and it just failed to act,” said Julia Curlee, a former Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) officer who specialized in the Middle East and China and also worked on the White House national security council during Trump’s first presidency. “It’s the latest episode of the president ignoring or not believing the intelligence that’s being provided to him.” Despite the intelligence concerns raised by his conduct, Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s chief executive on Monday following pressure from the White House and the company’s shareholders. Trump’s behaviour over the Nvidia affairs mirrors his conduct towards the war with Iran, Curlee argues, where he pressed ahead with military actions despite being forewarned of potential complications. Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran contradicted advice that the country’s Islamic regime had the resilience to withstand attempts to topple it and was likely to retaliate by closing the strait of Hormuz – predictions that were subsequently borne out. Trump’s dismissal of intelligence warnings in both cases recalls his comments at a 2018 summit with Vladimir Putin when he openly sided with the Russian president over US intelligence agencies, who had assessed that Russia had interfered in the 2016 presidential election. His indifference to intelligence work and the professionals who perform it appears to surpass that of previous administrations, even those who were accused of deliberately politicizing the practice – an accusation leveled at George W Bush following the 2003 invasion of Iraq. “There are other administrations that have ignored or or tried to politicize intelligence but I think the Trump administration stands alone in how little it seems to regard the intelligence analysis prepared to help the president make decisions,” said Curlee. “The best example of this is the run-up to the war in Iran, where the administration just truly shut out the warnings which have been there and were provided for many years about what the Iranians would do in the case of a war.” Trump’s administration has also fired agents for providing intelligence assessments at odds with the president’s own statements. Last year, Lt Gen Jeffrey Kruse, the head of the defense intelligence agency, was dismissed over a report that contradicted Trump’s claim that Iran’s nuclear sites had been “obliterated” by US strikes carried out in June 2025. “What makes them really different from, say, the Bush administration, is that even that administration did not publicly fire officers when they didn’t provide information the president wanted to hear,” said Curlee, who also served on the White House national security council under Trump and Joe Biden. “I feel pretty strongly that the fault of the Iran war lies at this refusal to listen to the intelligence community.” Curlee said the Chinese acquisition of the Nvidia chips compared in strategic significance to the case of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg , a US couple who were executed after being convicted of passing on atomic secrets to the Soviet Union in the early years of the cold war. That made official indifference to the intelligence discovery all the more remarkable, she argued. “This is a technology at the heart of the strategic competition with our primary competitor in the world, and at an industrial scale, they managed to divert chips from our leading hardware company,” she said. “It’s a terrible thing that’s occurred and we can’t undo that. But uncovering it and stopping it was done at least over a year ago. If the policymaker then refuses to do their to do their job, there’s nothing the intelligence community can do about that.” The administration’s stance has drawn further scrutiny by deciding not to provide a “defensive briefing” to Jensen Huang about the discovery. “Before public accusations and scandals, it used to be accepted practice for someone to pull the American target aside for a man-to-man chat – to tell him to think with the head between his shoulders,” said Fulton Armstrong, a former CIA analyst specializing in Latin America who also has experience in Taiwan. “The chat might even include discussion of feeding the foreigner some disinformation. It seems that four years of Trump first presidency, four years of do-nothingism with Biden, and now almost two years of Trump II have so deeply changed the intel community that practical solutions are no longer allowed.” No explanation has been provided for the failure to warn Huang – thus allowing him to continue his relationship with Alice Huang. He was also allowed to maintain his already close access to Trump. Curlee said it was a “policy decision [rather than] an intelligence decision.” She added “It is to me a very unusual suspect decision to let something like this go on for as long as it apparently did, without at minimum protecting this US citizen, who is the object of of a Chinese spy operation.” Fevered speculation has swirled over whether Alice Huang may have been part of a “honey trap” operation set by China’s intelligence services to lure Jensen Huang into a close business relationship that would entice him into vast amounts of Nvidia’s coveted chips to a company which would them to pass them to China, subverting American law. China’s sprawling Ministry of State Security [MSS] is believed to use the technique, which most western intelligence agencies publicly insist they do not use, on the grounds that is unethical and potentially counterproductive, because it often depends on blackmail. But analysts doubt that it occurred in this instance. Alice Huang, they suggest, could have disclosed the relationship to Chinese agents after it began because she was legally obliged to do so under China’s catch-all intelligence law, which legally obliges the country’s citizens to “cooperate” with security services on matters defined as “national security”. That term has a much broader definition under China’s laws than in most western countries, and can cover commercial and economic development issues. Frank Montoya, a retired Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agent who specialized on China, said a straightforward “honey trap” was unlikely. “I don’t think that it was it was mapped out specifically where the MSS officer said we’re going to find this person and we’re going to set her up for business and then target her against against the CEO of [Nvidia],” he said. “There was a confluence of opportunities. She’s very ambitious, very smart and she has this idea, and doesn’t necessarily brings it to the MSS, but is talking to somebody else. She has connections in the party, and she’s talking to somebody else, and then somebody else talks to the MSS and says, ‘hey, let’s see if we can take advantage of that’.” He added: “This was a multi-billion dollar purchase [of Nvidia chips]. There’s no way the MSS alone can fund that. They’re going to need somebody higher up [in the Chinese communist party] to not only approve that but to provide the money when the deal is made.” The operation, Montoya said, bore the hallmarks of the Chinese espionage approach, which he described as “whole of government” and lacking the “clandestinity” of traditional spy craft. Alice Huang would have drawn the attention of US intelligence agencies through Megaspeed’s mass purchase of Nvidia chips, and because it rented out services from its Singapore data centers to Chinese AI companies, Curlew argues. The intimate nature of her relationship with Jensen Huang, and her links to Chinese intelligence is thought to have been discovered through surveillance of her phone, almost certainly carried out by the National Security Agency. Trump has dismissed the case’s importance, saying he does not believe US national security was threatened and telling Fox News: “We spy on China. They spy on us.” He later told reporters that he raised the matter only briefly when he met China’s president, Xi Jinping, at last week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering Shenzhen. It is an attitude Curlee lamented as disdainful of intelligence as a whole. “We are spending tens of billions of dollars and people put their lives in jeopardy to collect information at great personal risk so that our leaders have decision-advantage, the ability to anticipate crises around the corner and can respond to foreign threats,” she said. “If the president can’t be bothered to listen to his intelligence community then what is what is the point of it all?” Explore more on these topics Nvidia Jensen Huang Donald Trump US politics Trump administration US national security Espionage analysis Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK US politics World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine Football Newsletters Business Environment UK politics Science Tech Global development Obituaries

Photograph: lisegagne/Getty Images Florida Thanksgiving meal in Florida leads to mass food poisoning incident Local media reported that 18 people fell ill after attending a Thanksgiving lunch at a medical center headquarters Guardian staff Fri 27 Nov 2026 08.41 EST Last modified on Fri 27 Nov 2026 10.48 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Thanksgiving meal in Florida triggered a bout of food poisoning so bad that local emergency officials said it was a “mass casualty” event as numerous stricken diners were sent to hospital. Local media reported that 18 people at the Leon Medical Center headquarters in Doral fell ill due to possible food poisoning after attending the center’s annual Thanksgiving lunch on Wednesday. Miami-Dade fire rescue crews who received reports of the possible food poisoning said the call was upgraded to a “ mass casualty incident ” after 15 of those who fell ill required hospitalization, the Miami Herald reported. In a statement to NBC Miami Leon Medical Center said: “Some of the staff began to experience gastrointestinal symptoms shortly after the luncheon and required treatment.” “We continue to work with the caterers to determine, if possible, the cause and continue to provide support to our staff and their families.” No patients at the center were affected. Investigations are continuing as to the exact cause and nature of the food poisoning.
